Treat Marina applet requests as permission to publish (#8926)

A request to build or update a Marina applet now authorizes publishing
it, including schema migrations and data loading needed for the
requested behavior. The skill previously required a separate explicit
request for each external write, leaving a validated applet unpublished
until the user confirmed again.

Requests for local-only work, drafts, or review before publication still
limit that authorization. Rollback, archive, and unrelated data
mutations remain scoped to the user's authorization.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iac] Let Marina deployments manage scheduler jobs (#8924)

Grant project-level `roles/cloudscheduler.admin` on `hai-gcp-models` to
`marin-cd-cloud-run-deploy@hai-gcp-models.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
Marina's Pulumi program creates, updates, and deletes Scheduler triggers
as app-declared runners change. [Merged-main rollout
33920055992](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33920055992)
failed on missing `cloudscheduler.jobs.create` and required a manual
owner recovery.

Cloud Scheduler Admin is Google's narrowest predefined role containing
the create, update, and delete permissions needed to reconcile the
trigger lifecycle. The grant can manage every Scheduler job in the
project; Google does not provide resource-level IAM for individual
Scheduler jobs. The current jobs and application stack are converged, so
applying this change should add only the IAM binding and let CI manage
later runner changes.

A reviewer should run the `review-grant` workflow, then apply the
`marin` Pulumi stack. The failure and recovery are recorded in
https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/339.

[grafana] Split inference overview from diagnostics (#8921)

Split inference telemetry into linked overview and diagnostics
dashboards. The overview shows progress, response speed, queueing, cache
pressure, and telemetry health. Diagnostics adds engine comparisons,
latency stages and tails, and output lengths. Diagnostics retains the
existing `marin-inference` UID and all original panel IDs, so old panel
links still work. Links between the two views retain the selected serve
and time range.

Separate request counts from tokens per engine iteration, and fleet
throughput from per-request token latency. Show finished-request rates
by outcome without treating them as arrival demand. Missing observations
remain missing. The descriptions explain why draining requests alone
cannot distinguish an intentional RL batch barrier from upstream
starvation.

Read existing Finelog records only: no new telemetry, vLLM changes, or
GPU experiments. Extend the shared bounded query and reuse panel
fragments. Expand histogram statistics in one pass to avoid repeating
the aggregation in Finelog's query plan.

All 256 Grafana tests pass. Candidate queries complete against both the
historical Snowball run and a recent run with per-engine telemetry. The
real Grafana Infinity datasource accepts every panel target, and browser
previews render both dashboards with those query results. The 136
existing non-freshness rows match the historical baseline within
floating-point tolerance. Historical latency panels show no samples
where stored histograms cannot be attributed to individual engines.
These checks do not deploy the dashboards.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Publish dynamic applets (#8916)

Add `marina publish` and lifecycle commands for applets stored in
Postgres.
Marina's existing IAP policy gates both the publishing API and applet
requests.
Each applet receives a stable UUID. Each successful publish allocates
its next
revision and atomically selects it as current. Automatic retention keeps
the
current revision and the four highest-numbered alternatives. Files are
deduplicated across applets by digest and media type. Only the recorded
owner
or a user ID in `MARINA_APPLET_OPERATORS` can update, roll back, or
archive an
applet. Archive removes its routes and entry from Marina's app list but
preserves its schema and retained revisions; v1 has no restore
operation.

Give each applet a Postgres role that can write its own schema and
select from
schemas owned by checked-in and dynamic Marina apps. Browser-submitted
SQL
permits one statement with a 10-second timeout. Postgres bounds `SELECT`
and
read-only `WITH` results to 10,000 rows and a 5 MiB serialized JSON
payload
before transferring them; data-modifying `WITH` and mutation `RETURNING`
statements are rejected. The CLI also loads JSON, JSONL, CSV, and
Parquet tables
as DDL and DML through the same query endpoint.

An applet may ship a Python ASGI backend and a migration that runs in
the
publish transaction before activation. Any IAP-authorized caller can
create a
Python applet; only its owner or an operator can upload later revisions.
The `AppletServices` object passed to the backend supplies an engine
configured
for the applet's restricted database role. Uploaded Python remains
trusted: it
can create other clients from Marina's process environment and access
Cloud Run
filesystem, network, and service credentials. The separate
applets.marina.oa.dev origin exposes only `/a/*` routes and keeps
uploaded
JavaScript off Marina's main origin; it is not a process sandbox.

`marina publish DIR --local` starts disposable pgvector Postgres,
installs
`marina.provision_applet(uuid)` and the `marina.applets` registry
tables,
publishes through a loopback Marina process, and serves the immutable
revision
until Ctrl-C. The `marina-applet` repository skill uses this command as
its
default validation path. Local mode does not enable IAP and removes its
database container on exit.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Fail closed on object-storage errors (#8917)

Object-backed Finelog now fails closed when durable catalog state cannot
be interpreted or updated. Boot recovery rejects malformed live object
references, direct queries reject incomplete active schemas, legacy
eviction changes the live view only after its catalog mutation succeeds,
and scheduler and staging-cleanup errors are reported. Kubernetes passes
the configured object-cache limit into each server.

The object-store provider owns validated object locations for storage
and querying. Durable state transitions carry explicit queue, lease,
mutation, garbage-collection, migration, and work results, reducing
ambiguous state at recovery, registration, compaction, and maintenance
boundaries. Tests use shared fixtures and logical or condition-based
synchronization.

Catalog migration 0006 and the reserved protobuf slots remain unchanged
because their intermediate forms reached live catalogs before #8748
merged.

Fixes #8909
Fixes #8837
Fixes #8882

[codehealth] Run one bounded pull-request review (#8915)

Launch one correctness review per trusted pull request and stop
launching a
separate lint-catalog session. The `agentic-lint` label already records
the
required local catalog pass. In the two reported examples, local passes
at the
authors' initial commits emitted 13 findings for #8913 and 36 for #8914.
The
later CI reruns at subsequent heads posted another 6 and 10 findings.
Removing
the rerun trades that extra stochastic sample for half as many Loom
sessions
per pull request.

Define the review standard in `review-pr`: changed behavior must match
the pull
request's claims, follow scoped repository and testing policy, preserve
interfaces and invariants, avoid concrete maintainability obstacles, and
leave

longer
prescribes review-process topology. This removes the orchestration
fan-out that
left #8914's correctness session running without a completion marker.

The review profile requires a typed Loom result and archives idle
sessions
after the platform's 15-minute safety window instead of retaining them
for one
hour.

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
[nightshift] Fix CLI worker task_outputs drift and delete dead code (#8904)

`iris cluster create-slice` and `iris cluster worker-restart` each
rebuilt the
base worker config inline instead of calling `build_base_worker_config`,
the
helper the controller uses for autoscaled workers. Both inline copies
had
drifted by omitting `task_outputs`, so workers created or restarted from
the CLI
ran with `task_outputs=None` and silently captured no per-attempt output
archives, unlike autoscaler-provisioned workers in the same cluster.
Both call
sites now go through the helper, which leaves it as the only place
deciding what
the controller ships to a worker. The other fields are unchanged: the
CLI
resolves the controller address from `config.controller_address()`
before
falling back to provider discovery, and no cluster config sets
`defaults.worker.storage_prefix` or `auth_token`.

Levanter defined the stalled-training exit code 124 twice, as
`STALLED_TRAINING_EXIT_CODE` in the progress watchdog and `EXIT_STALL`
in
`recovery/types.py`, with a comment asserting the two must agree and
nothing
enforcing it. Had the watchdog's copy drifted, `classify_returncode`
would map a
stalled child to `FaultClass.HARD`, so the supervisor would propagate
the
failure instead of warm-restarting from the host snapshot. The watchdog
now
imports `EXIT_STALL` from the recovery module that already owns the
trainer/supervisor exit-code contract.

`marin/export/hf_upload.py` lost its only caller in #6649, which removed
the
`upload_dir_to_hf` ExecutorStep wrapper during the lazy-artifact
migration.
What remained was reachable only from the module's own `__main__` block,
which
pushes a scratch file to a personal Hugging Face repo. Checkpoint export
runs
through `marin/export/levanter_checkpoint.py`. The `InferenceBackend`
Protocol
in `marin/inference/backend.py` goes with it: it has no implementers or
annotations anywhere, since the concrete backends are selected by class.

In the Zephyr worker, `_finish_active_shard` copied counters into
`last_counters` and dropped the shard from `_active_shards` nine lines
later, so
the copy could never be read again, and the task thread rebuilt
`traceback.format_exc()` character by character through `"".join(...)`.
The
`shard_subprocess` docstring justified its separation from
`zephyr.runners` via
an `__init__ -> execution -> runners` import chain; there is no
`zephyr.execution` module and `zephyr/__init__.py` has had no imports
since
#7075. It now states the invariant that still holds, that the `-m`
target is a
leaf module nothing imports.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Add object-backed table storage (#8748)

Store versioned Finelog tables as immutable Parquet objects selected by
a conditionally updated table catalog. Canonical object IDs resolve
through an object-store interface, and the local cache mirrors the
`_finelog/tables/<table>/...` layout so an empty local store can recover
from HEAD and immutable catalogs.

Durable table state has one authority and one write path. Every mutation
— flush, compaction, index backfill, registration, activation, abort,
retire, forward cursor, tombstone — commits through a private per-table
controller that allocates a monotonic revision and carries a writer
fence; the compensating generation decrements are gone. Commits validate
the fence recorded in HEAD, so a stale server cannot advance a table
another process has claimed, and an ambiguous CAS resolves by re-reading
HEAD and comparing revision, fence, and state hash — commits roll
forward or fence, never back. Dropping a table publishes a durable
tombstone revision instead of deleting HEAD. Ingest is local-first: a
flush stages its sealed Parquet into the verified cache layout (pinned
against eviction) and commits the revision to the local catalog, which
acknowledges the write; uploading the staged objects and the fenced HEAD
swap run on the publication path, attempted immediately and retried by
maintenance, so a sustained remote outage delays publication without
blocking ingest. The trade-off is explicit: between local ack and
publication the tail exists only on that node's disk, so a fence steal
or node loss can drop acknowledged-but-unpublished rows. Recovery is
metadata-only: bootstrap loads state, claims the fence, and seeds
sequence numbers without downloading data or adopting cached files;
SQLite is a projection for object-backed tables and remains the
authority only for legacy tables. The published high-water mark carries
the legacy allocator watermark, publishes clamp it monotone across
revisions (retirement deletes the legacy rows the aggregate is computed
from), and recovery seeds the allocator past it, so a recovered writer
never reissues a sequence number.

Fixes #8737
Fixes #8784

Incident record: [migrated log tail queries time out after
restart](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/337)

Related review debt: #8909

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Shared service for Echo, EvalDash, and TaskTrove (#8867)

Marina is one IAP-gated Cloud Run service hosting Marin's small internal
web apps. Each app is a directory under `infra/marina/apps/` with an
`app.toml` and a Vue frontend served at `/<name>/`; a Python app adds
`create_api(services)`, mounted at `/<name>/api/` behind the kernel's
authentication, and `migrate(engine)`, run against the app's own schema
of the shared `marina` database at the end of every deploy. Echo,
EvalDash, and TaskTrove are ported; `infra/echo` and `infra/evaldash`
are removed. The shared kit under `infra/marina/web` gives every app the
same tokens, top bar with app switcher and identity chip, and Markdown
rendering.

App data moves out of the repository to a data root, `gs://marin-marina`
in production and `infra/marina/.data` locally, served at
`/<app>/data/`. Journeys are browser walks that double as tests: a
Playwright DSL (visit, sees, click, fill, offers, reads, api, shoot,
widths) against an in-process kernel, with screenshots and optional
video, run by `marina journey`. Each app ships journeys; page errors and
failed API calls fail the walk.

Deployment is one stack: the `marina` database on `marin-metadata`, the
bucket, the service (4 CPU, 4 GiB, one warm instance, up to four), a
`marina-migrate` job executed after each image change, and Echo's sync
as a scheduled job on the same image and service account, so there is a
single database user and no grant migrations. `marina.oa.dev`,
`echo.oa.dev`, and `evaldash.oa.dev` all map to the service. The two old
hosts redirect into their app on `marina.oa.dev` rather than serving it
at their own root, so the apps sit in one URL space: serving on the
alias too would put every page at two origins, and a root-relative link
from one app to another would pick up the alias's prefix — `/evaldash/`
on `echo.oa.dev` became `/echo/evaldash/`. Every API route keeps its
path, method, and response model, and a vanity host still serves them:
`echo.oa.dev/api/...` is routed straight to the mounted API rather than
redirected, because requests and curl drop the Authorization header
across a cross-origin redirect and the retry would come back as IAP's
sign-in page with status 200. Only pages redirect. An app may not be
named for a route the kernel answers itself (`api`, `healthz`); startup
refuses rather than let the app silently lose those paths. IAM is one
target in the `marin` stack. `marina migrate --reader
eng-all@openathena.ai` grants the Cloud SQL group login people query
with USAGE and SELECT on every schema, which is what Echo's
`m0003_openathena_grants.py` did before it was deleted. The codehealth
workbench keeps its `context` database and Loom login, now declared by
this stack, and creates its tables with `refinement_tools.py
init-schema` instead of an Echo migration.

The rollout ran before merge rather than after, so this lands against
infrastructure that is already in its final state. Marina is live and
serving all three hosts; Echo's 12 tables and EvalDash's 8 were copied
out of the `context` and `evals` databases into the `marina` schemas,
roughly 216k rows and 2.2 GB, and matched the source counts at copy
time. The copy took 79 minutes, almost all of it pgvector index
maintenance on `chunks` and `repository_file_chunks`. A second additive
pass after the domains moved added no rows, so no writes were lost in
the switch. The `marin-echo` and `marin-evaldash` stacks are destroyed
and removed, and the `marin` stack is applied. The source tables in
`evals` and `context` are left intact.

Verified locally: 169 kernel and app tests against a throwaway pgvector
container, 9 journeys across the three apps with screenshots, pyrefly,
and lint. Echo's search benchmark, whose 80 graded queries move with the
app, scores the deployed service at MRR@10 0.834, nDCG@10 0.832, hit
rate 0.965, judgment recall 0.805, and no-answer accuracy 0.714 on the
dev split -- the range `benchmarks/README.md` records for the July
ranking work, over a corpus that has grown since. Collect serially:
concurrent queries scale Cloud Run out and each new instance loads the
ONNX models on its first search.

Dropped: Echo's grant migration chain, EvalDash's dark-mode toggle (it
follows the system now). EvalDash's ingest loops start on the first
request because lifespan events do not propagate through a Starlette
mount, which is also why the service holds CPU between requests; moving
ingest into a scheduled job would let it fall back to request-based CPU.
The two apps keep separate migration ledgers, and only EvalDash's runner
locks and rejects unknown migration names; a shared one is a follow-up.
Echo keeps its own `marked`/DOMPurify renderer rather than the kit's
`Prose`, which refuses `v-html` because it draws text a model wrote: of
332 wiki entries, 17 use tables and 6 use nested lists, neither of which
the kit's subset renderer draws. EvalDash still rejects 39 eval runs
whose serve config carries fields its record schema forbids, unchanged
from before the port and tracked in #8885.

[iris] Isolate XLA autotune caches by process (#8896)

Give each multigpu process its own node-local XLA per-fusion autotune
directory. The hero continuation failed while saving checkpoint step
58,181 because three ranks sharing `/cache/xla/per-fusion-autotune` lost
their temporary `.textproto` files during XLA cache insertion. The other
ranks then aborted through JAX fate sharing, and Iris retried the
176-task gang.

This reapplies [commit
61742bfa](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/61742bfa2a512daff91cbd91e9e769197151dfde),
developed during [MoK EP64
debugging](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8244#issuecomment-5290127992),
to the current FineStore-backed cache implementation. Disabling the
cache previously left a rack compiling for fifteen minutes without
reaching a step, so the cache remains enabled and writers are isolated
by global process index.

The JAX-init test file passes all 27 cases, including separate paths for
a node's local leader and sibling rank. The broader affected-test
selection passes 524 tests with 5 skips.

Part of #8244

commits.message:
[grafana] Read embedded vLLM telemetry (#8872)

The existing `/v1/vllm/overview` path and inference dashboard read
standalone serving rows with `service=vllm` and trainer-embedded rows
with `service=marinskyrl, metric_source=vllm`. Requiring both embedded
labels excludes Ray metrics from the same trainer process. Embedded data
keeps the requested 15-second bins. Standalone data stays at its
60-second scrape floor so sparse counter deltas are not presented as
denser samples.

For embedded rows, the producer's physical-engine UUID is the stable
`engine` label; local placement remains `engine_index`. Gauges,
histograms, and freshness use that UUID across step changes. A live
engine can no longer hide a stopped peer that shares its trainer
resource. Standalone freshness remains keyed by its existing resource
identity. Embedded histograms require `engine_index`, which rejects
legacy actor-local identities. Iteration occupancy joins saturation and
time-resolved TPOT joins latency without changing the nine-section,
ten-column API contract.

One 77-line test follows the checked-in dashboard target through the
HTTP route, generated SQL, DuckDB, and JSON. It covers 77 of 83
executable lines in `vllm_observability.py` (93%) and checks
representative rate, outcome, TPOT, saturation, and stopped-versus-live
freshness values. The stopped/live case failed before the fix as one
shared fresh resource. The complete Grafana suite passes 244 tests.

The final SQL ran through Finelog for a 150-second embedded window and a
standalone control. Both returned the ordered ten-column schema. The
standalone control retained one resource freshness row, all nine
sections, and 22 non-null latency rows. The historical embedded run
predates the companion producer's corrected stable identity, so a new
instrumented run is still required for that runtime proof.

Companion MarinSkyRL producer:
https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/502. The separate
`rl_runs.json` dashboard must map its selected run to the API identity
field and value; that wiring is outside this change.

Part of #8562.
